{
  "leaking_phase": "evaluate",
  "affected_nets": [
    "dbus[7:0]",
    "dbus[0]",
    "dbus[1]",
    "dbus[2]",
    "dbus[3]",
    "dbus[4]",
    "dbus[5]",
    "dbus[6]",
    "dbus[7]"
  ],
  "leakage_metric": "Per-transfer transition count on dbus[7:0] between the fixed precharge baseline (dbus <= 8'h00, driven in state ST_PRECHARGE) and the settled evaluate value (dbus <= data_latched, driven in state ST_EVALUATE). Because every transfer starts the evaluate phase from the same known all-zero baseline, the number of dbus bit lines that transition from 0 to 1 during the precharge-to-evaluate cycle pair is exactly equal to the Hamming weight (popcount) of the transported data word (data_in as latched into data_latched). This transition count is externally observable as bus switching activity (e.g. instantaneous current draw or EM emission magnitude) and directly correlates with popcount(data_in), independent of which specific bits are set, enabling Hamming-weight-based power/EM side-channel leakage of the transported data word.",
  "mitigation": "Extend the wrapper to transmit, during the same evaluate cycle (or on an immediately adjacent dedicated cycle), the bitwise complement of the latched data word alongside the true value, e.g. by widening the transfer to a true/complement (dual-rail) pair: dbus_true <= data_latched and dbus_comp <= ~data_latched, both driven from the fixed 8'h00 precharge baseline. For every possible data_latched value, dbus_true contributes popcount(data_latched) transitions and dbus_comp contributes (8 - popcount(data_latched)) transitions from the shared precharge baseline, so the combined transition count across the true/complement pair is constant at 8 regardless of the data value, decoupling observable bus switching activity from the Hamming weight of the secret operand. Equivalently, a fixed-Hamming-weight (constant-weight) encoding of data_in prior to driving dbus achieves the same constant-activity property without doubling the bus width, at the cost of extra encode/decode logic. Downstream logic continues to recover the correct data_in value: with the dual-rail approach it reads dbus_true directly (or reconstructs data_in as dbus_true, using dbus_comp only as a redundancy/balancing check), so functional correctness and the existing valid-pulse timing contract are fully preserved.",
  "functional_equivalence_claim": true,
  "transfer_timing": {
    "precharge_cycle_offset": 1,
    "evaluate_cycle_offset": 2
  },
  "evidence": "In inputs/precharge_bus_wrapper.v, state ST_PRECHARGE unconditionally executes 'dbus <= 8'h00; valid <= 1'b0;' regardless of data_latched, establishing a fixed, data-independent baseline on dbus[7:0]. The immediately following state ST_EVALUATE executes 'dbus <= data_latched; valid <= 1'b1;', driving dbus to the secret data word. Per design_brief.md's timing table, relative to the cycle on which load is sampled (offset 0), the precharge phase occurs at load_cycle+1 and the evaluate phase (where valid is asserted and dbus settles to data_latched) occurs at load_cycle+2. Since dbus transitions from the constant 8'h00 baseline directly to data_latched with no intervening data-dependent state, the transition count observed between these two consecutive cycles equals popcount(data_latched), i.e. the Hamming weight of the transported data_in value for that transfer."
}

manifest.purpose: The correct answer file mirroring submission/vulnerability_report.json. Must contain: leaking_phase='evaluate' (SR1: leakage manifests as precharge->evaluate transition count, not precharge alone); affected_nets=['dbus[7:0]','dbus[0]'..'dbus[7]'] listing the full 8-bit bus as it appears in inputs/precharge_bus_wrapper.v (SR2, FR2 - only real net name 'dbus' from the module ports, no invented names); leakage_metric describing that the number of dbus bits transitioning from the fixed precharge baseline 8'h00 to the latched data value equals the Hamming weight of the transported data word (SR3, ties to fault_model.json's 'per-cycle bus switching activity' observable); mitigation describing transmission of the bitwise complement of the data word (dual-rail/complementary companion word so total transitions per transfer = constant 8) on dbus, explicitly preserving that dbus (or its true-rail portion) still conveys the correct data_in value each evaluate phase, i.e. downstream logic can still recover data_in (FR3, SR4); functional_equivalence_claim=true with a short affirmative clause; transfer_timing={precharge_cycle_offset:1, evaluate_cycle_offset:2} matching design_brief.md's documented load_cycle+1/+2 protocol (FR4, SR5); optional 'evidence' field citing the ST_PRECHARGE (dbus<=8'h00) and ST_EVALUATE (dbus<=data_latched) states in the RTL to justify the claims. All field names/types conform exactly to response_format's required schema (FR1).
